analysis.investment_thesis: A small-cap Indian defense play with genuine 45%+ earnings growth riding the indigenization wave, but the PEG of ~1.6 (P/E 73 / growth 45%) is stretched and cash conversion is broken — OCF positive only 1 of last 4 years. The story is right but the price and working-capital drag keep this from being a clean Lynch fast-grower buy.
key_strengths: Revenue 3Y CAGR of 45.8% (47→146 Cr) with earnings growing in lockstep — fast grower credentials intact.
Promoter holding 68.06% signals strong skin-in-the-game; ROCE of 23.65% shows capital efficiency.
Aerospace & Defense tailwind visible from the consumer/policy lens — Make-in-India order book expanding for years.
key_risks: Free cash flow deeply negative (-29, -43, -8 Cr last 3Y) — growth is being funded, not self-sustaining.
PEG ~1.6 and P/B 10.9 leave no margin of safety if growth decelerates even mildly.
Tiny 1,516 Cr market cap with 0.01% FII / 0.66% DII ownership — illiquid, prone to sharp re-ratings.
red_flags: OCF negative in 3 of last 4 years despite rising reported profits — classic working-capital trap.
Equity jumped from 25→126 Cr in FY24 (dilution/QIP) — per-share growth lower than headline.
P/E of 73 on a 24 Cr profit base — any single contract slip re-rates this violently.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
What's the story? Small Indian defense supplier compounding topline at 45%+ with ROCE in the mid-20s, riding a multi-year indigenization tailwind I can see from the newspapers. That's a genuine fast-grower setup, and promoters owning 68% tells me management is betting on themselves. On paper this should be ten-bagger territory — 146 Cr revenue in a sector where peers are 10-50x that size means plenty of runway.

But the numbers force me to slow down. P/E 73 against 45% growth gives a PEG ~1.6 — above my 1.0 comfort zone. Worse, operating cash flow is -3 Cr in FY25 and FCF has been negative three years running, meaning the "profits" are tied up in receivables and inventory typical of defense order-book businesses. They funded the build-out with a big equity raise (equity 25→126 Cr in FY24), so per-share economics lag the headlines. I want to own this story, but not at this price — I'd wait for either (a) the stock to cool 25-30% bringing PEG near 1.0, or (b) two consecutive quarters of positive OCF proving the growth actually converts to cash. Until then, HOLD and watch.
